summary: Engine.T is mutable and explicitly not thread safe; its bus dictionaries, envelope state and listener/voice observations require one caller-owned drive thread. Host backends likewise do not promise concurrent Play safety, and OpenAL context ownership is thread sensitive. Audio.Elmish provides a command adapter but does not by itself prove those calls execute on the engine's owning thread. Create a mixing sink once; recreating it every frame discards gains/envelopes. createSink owns elapsed wall time, so pauses/stalls can complete fades; createSinkWith lets a product supply its deterministic/pause-aware dt. The contract describes these limitations; source inspection here ran no device or concurrency qualification.
title: Mixing engine and backend require caller-owned single-thread drive
